title: A rate is reported outside the range a rate can take
detects: A metric whose own units say `proportion` carrying a value below 0 or above 1. A proportion is a count divided by a total, so it cannot be negative and cannot exceed one. A number outside that range is not a measurement that came out badly; it is arithmetic that went wrong, a sign error, a division by the wrong denominator, or a field carrying something other than what its name says.
incident: Ours, 2026-09-17. A hostile reviewer working from an installed wheel fed this checker an artefact carrying a refusal rate of -0.5 and a Heretic keyword rate of 1.5, and it reported `0 finding(s)`. The report was accurate and the gap was coverage: all three checks that existed applied to that document and none of them fired, because not one of them asked whether a number was possible. The skip machinery was working; there was simply nothing to skip. That is the more uncomfortable version, because it means the green was earned under the rules as written. The same reviewer observed that this checker ships as a GitHub Action and a pre-commit hook, so that green was being trusted in CI.
remedy: Find the arithmetic. A negative rate is usually a subtraction done in the wrong order or a delta stored in a field that names an absolute rate; a rate above one is usually a count used where a proportion belongs, or a percentage written into a field whose units are a fraction. Do not clamp it: the number is evidence of the bug and clamping destroys the evidence while leaving the bug.
false_positive: A harness that legitimately records a signed CHANGE in a rate under units `proportion` would fire here, and it would be right to, because a delta and a rate should not share units. If your artefact does that, the fix is to give the delta its own units rather than to ignore the finding. This check cannot fire on a metric whose units are absent or say anything other than `proportion`, so a harness that does not record units escapes it entirely, which is a gap in coverage rather than a reason to widen the rule. Such an artefact is SKIPPED rather than passed, since 2026-09-21: `applies_to` used to claim any document carrying a metrics block at all, so a coherence figure in nats-per-token was examined by a check that could not possibly speak about it and came back clean. The sentence above admitted the rule could not fire; the applicability did not, and a reader counting examined checks was being told a question had been asked.
